summary.text: 水 means “water” and began as a drawing of flowing water. A central stream with droplets alongside it became the compact modern form. When used beside another component, 水 often takes the familiar three-dot form 氵; the two shapes represent the same water component.

formation.text: Flowing water represented by a whole picture.

components.text: The central stroke and surrounding marks form one water image. The side marks are described as droplets, not separate meaning or sound components.

history.text: Early versions vary in the number of droplets and strokes. Component forms can concentrate on the droplets, helping explain the later compressed 氵 form. Another written variant is 氺. Variation in these water shapes should not be mistaken for the addition of unrelated components.
